main_text.l: ste Euseb. Lib. 6. Hist. Eccles. Cap. 3. Postea autem in
Palæstinam se contulit Origenes, & Cæsareæ ludum ape-
ruit, ubi licet nondum Presbyterij gradu potitus esset, ab
Episcopis, qui ibi erant, ad disputandum, & ad sacras
etiam Scripturas in communi Ecclesiæ conventu aperien-
das admissus est. Posterior hæc libertas concionandi co-
ram populo displicuit Demetrio, Episcopo Alexandri-
no, sed factum suum in concedenda illa libertate Alexan-
Episcoporum, qui Laicos quosdam, habiles & idoneos ad
præbendum fratribus adjumentum, hortati fuerant ut
populum in verbo instituerent, τῷ λαῷ συνομιλεῖν
[?]: ut scribit Eusebius Lib. 6. Hist. Cap. 13. x. Quamvis hac
quidem in parte fortasse non male senserit DEMETRIUS.

page.notes: The Greek phrase at the line end is only partly legible and is marked [?]. The printed "Euseb" and similar forms keep the printer's long-s spelling as plain s where relevant. "DEMETRIUS" has its final letters in a stylised form; the reading is likely. The "CAP." at the foot is shown as printed, with no number following.
